source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ כָּל־שִׁבְטֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד חֶבְר֑וֹנָה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנְנ֛וּ עַצְמְךָ֥ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ֖ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came all [the] tribes of Israel to David to Hebron, and said, saying, Here we, your bone and your flesh [are] we.

en.L: And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we [are] your bone and your flesh.
en.B: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron. "Look," they told him, "we are your own bone and flesh.
en.R: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron. They said, "We are your own relatives.

es.L: Y vinieron todas las tribus de Israel a David en Hebrón y dijeron: «He aquí que nosotros [somos] tu hueso y tu carne.
es.B: Entonces todas las tribus de Israel vinieron a David en Hebrón. «Mira», le dijeron, «somos tu propio hueso y tu propia carne.
es.R: Entonces todas las tribus de Israel vinieron a ver a David en Hebrón. Le dijeron: «Somos tus propios parientes.

fr.L: Et toutes les tribus d’Israël vinrent auprès de David à Hébron, et dirent : « Voici, nous [sommes] tes os et ta chair.
fr.B: Alors toutes les tribus d’Israël vinrent trouver David à Hébron. « Vois, lui dirent-elles, nous sommes de tes os et de ta chair.
fr.R: Alors toutes les tribus d’Israël sont venues voir David à Hébron. Elles lui ont dit : « Nous sommes de ta propre famille.

vi.L: Tất cả các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên đến cùng Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn và nói: "Kìa, chúng tôi là xương thịt của ngài.
vi.B: Bấy giờ tất cả các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn và thưa: "Chúng tôi đây là cốt nhục của ngài.
vi.R: Rồi tất cả các chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn. Họ nói: "Chúng tôi là bà con ruột thịt của ngài.

decisions.choice: your bone and your flesh: your own kin, people of the same family
decisions.reason: To be someone's bone and flesh is to be closely related to him (Genesis 2:23; 29:14; Judges 9:2). The northern tribes remind David that they are not strangers: they belong to the same people, descended from the same ancestor, Israel.

decisions.choice: all the tribes came: the north now accepts David, after the war with Saul's house
decisions.reason: Since Saul's death David had been king of Judah alone at Hebron (2:4, 11), while Saul's son Ish-bosheth reigned over the other tribes (2:8-10). With Abner and Ish-bosheth both dead (3:27; 4:5-12), the rest of Israel turns to David.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 11:1-3 retells verses 1-3
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells the same scene almost word for word, but has "all Israel gathered to David" for "all the tribes of Israel came", and adds at the end that the anointing followed the word of the LORD through Samuel. Chronicles also leaves out the years at Hebron (verses 4-5) and goes straight to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: your own relatives
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of bone and flesh by its meaning, family kinship.

decisions.choice: "xương thịt" (L); "cốt nhục" (B); "bà con ruột thịt" (R)
decisions.reason: Your own kin (meaning decision); Vietnamese "cốt nhục" is itself bone and flesh, so Balanced keeps the picture in a natural word and Readable says kin.

decisions.choice: the tribes call David "ngài" and themselves "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: They speak before they have made him their king (verse 3), as a people to a great leader.

source.text: גַּם־אֶתְמ֣וֹל גַּם־שִׁלְשׁ֗וֹם בִּהְי֨וֹת שָׁא֥וּל מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אַתָּ֗ה הָיִ֛יתָ הַמּוֹצִ֥יא וְהַמֵּבִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לְךָ֗ אַתָּ֨ה תִרְעֶ֤ה אֶת־עַמִּי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאַתָּ֛ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְנָגִ֖יד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Both yesterday, both three days ago, when was Saul king over us, you were the [one] leading out and the [one] bringing in Israel; and said Yahweh to you, You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be for ruler over Israel.

en.L: Both yesterday and the day before, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought [it] in. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to you, 'You will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, and you will be ruler over Israel.'"
en.B: In times past, even while Saul reigned over us, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to you, 'You are the one who will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; you will become ruler over Israel.'"
en.R: Even when Saul was our king, you were the one who led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told you, 'You will be the shepherd of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. You will be the leader of Israel.'"

es.L: Tanto ayer como anteayer, cuando Saúl era rey sobre nosotros, tú eras el que sacaba y metía a Israel. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dijo: “Tú pastorearás a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel, y tú serás gobernante sobre Israel”».
es.B: En tiempos pasados, aun cuando Saúl reinaba sobre nosotros, tú eras quien sacaba a Israel a la batalla y lo traía de vuelta. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dijo: “Tú eres quien pastoreará a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel; tú serás gobernante sobre Israel”».
es.R: Aun cuando Saúl era nuestro rey, tú eras el que dirigía al ejército de Israel en la guerra y lo traía de regreso. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te dijo: “Tú serás el pastor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel. Tú serás el líder de Israel”».

fr.L: Hier comme avant-hier, quand Saül était roi sur nous, c’est toi qui faisais sortir et qui faisais rentrer Israël. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a dit : “C’est toi qui feras paître {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël, et c’est toi qui seras chef sur Israël.” »
fr.B: Autrefois déjà, quand Saül régnait sur nous, c’est toi qui conduisais Israël au combat et qui le ramenais. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a dit : “C’est toi qui seras le berger de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël ; tu deviendras chef d’Israël.” »
fr.R: Même quand Saül était notre roi, c’est toi qui menais l’armée d’Israël au combat et qui la ramenais à la maison. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a dit : “Tu seras le berger de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël. Tu seras le chef d’Israël.” »

vi.L: Cả hôm qua lẫn hôm trước, khi Sau-lơ làm vua trên chúng tôi, chính ngài là người dẫn Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đi và đưa [họ] về. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với ngài: 'Ngươi sẽ chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ngươi sẽ làm người lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên.'"
vi.B: Trước đây, ngay khi Sau-lơ còn làm vua chúng tôi, chính ngài là người dẫn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra trận và đưa họ trở về. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với ngài: 'Chính con sẽ chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; con sẽ làm người lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên.'"
vi.R: Ngay khi Sau-lơ còn làm vua chúng tôi, chính ngài là người dẫn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra trận và đưa họ về nhà. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với ngài: 'Con sẽ là người chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Con sẽ là người lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên.'"

decisions.choice: yesterday and three days ago: in the past, for some time now
decisions.reason: The pair of time words is a Hebrew way of saying "before now" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:8; 1 Samuel 19:7). The elders mean that David's leadership is nothing new.

decisions.choice: leading out and bringing in: leading the army to war and home again
decisions.reason: To lead out and bring in is said of a commander who takes his men into battle and brings them back (Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11). It recalls 1 Samuel 18:13, 16, where all Israel and Judah loved David because he went out and came in before them.

decisions.choice: shepherd my people; ruler: the king cares for a people that belongs to God
decisions.reason: The verb "shepherd" pictures a king who guards and feeds a flock that is not his own: the people are Yahweh's ("my people"). David was taken from the sheep (1 Samuel 16:11; Psalm 78:70-72). "Ruler" is the word used for a leader appointed by God, as for Saul in 1 Samuel 9:16 and for David in 1 Samuel 13:14 and 25:30.

decisions.choice: you were the one who led out and brought in: the same sense in both spellings
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters spell "you were" and the two words for "the one who led out" and "the one who brought in" in an unusual way, and the scribes' marginal note gives the ordinary forms to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: out to battle and brought them back (Balanced); led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom of going out and coming in refers to, the leading of troops in war, so that the elders' point is clear.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word rendered "ruler", as in the rest of these books.

decisions.choice: chef (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note sets for *nagid*: "chef" serves at every level, where the English has "ruler" and "leader".

decisions.choice: "gobernante" (L, B); "líder" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for nagid: "gobernante" at Literal and Balanced, "líder" at Readable, for the whole of 2 Samuel.

decisions.choice: "người lãnh đạo" for *nagid* at every level
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's word for *nagid*; God calls David "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R), as the Genesis note sets.

source.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ כָּל־זִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹ֣ת לָהֶם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ דָּוִ֥ד בְּרִ֛ית בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּמְשְׁח֧וּ אֶת־דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came all [the] elders of Israel to the king to Hebron, and cut for them the king David a covenant in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David for king over Israel.

en.L: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they anointed David [as] king over Israel.
en.B: When all the elders of Israel had come to the king in Hebron, King David made a covenant with them there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they anointed David king over Israel.
en.R: All the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. There David made a covenant with them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they poured oil on his head to make him king over Israel.

es.L: Y vinieron todos los ancianos de Israel al rey en Hebrón, y el rey David hizo pacto con ellos en Hebrón delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; y ungieron a David [como] rey sobre Israel.
es.B: Cuando todos los ancianos de Israel llegaron ante el rey en Hebrón, el rey David hizo un pacto con ellos allí, en presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ungieron a David como rey sobre Israel.
es.R: Todos los líderes de Israel vinieron a ver al rey David en Hebrón. Allí David hizo un pacto con ellos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ellos le derramaron aceite sobre la cabeza para hacerlo rey de Israel.

fr.L: Et tous les anciens d’Israël vinrent auprès du roi à Hébron, et le roi David conclut avec eux une alliance à Hébron devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; et ils oignirent David [comme] roi sur Israël.
fr.B: Quand tous les anciens d’Israël furent venus auprès du roi à Hébron, le roi David conclut avec eux une alliance en ce lieu, en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils oignirent David comme roi sur Israël.
fr.R: Tous les chefs d’Israël sont venus voir le roi David à Hébron. Là, David a fait une alliance avec eux devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils lui ont versé de l’huile sur la tête pour faire de lui le roi d’Israël.

vi.L: Tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến cùng vua tại Hếp-rôn, và vua Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ tại Hếp-rôn trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; rồi họ xức dầu cho Đa-vít làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Khi tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua tại Hếp-rôn, vua Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ tại đó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ xức dầu cho Đa-vít làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn. Tại đó Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ đổ dầu trên đầu ông để lập ông làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên.

decisions.choice: made a covenant with them: a binding agreement between the king and the people
decisions.reason: The verb is literally "cut", the usual word for making a covenant. A covenant between a king and his people set out what each owed the other, under oath (1 Samuel 10:25; 2 Kings 11:17). The elders accept David as king, and David binds himself to them.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: in his presence, with him as witness
decisions.reason: An agreement made "before Yahweh" was made solemnly, with God called on to see it and to hold both sides to it (1 Samuel 23:18).

decisions.choice: they anointed David: the third time David is anointed
decisions.reason: Samuel anointed David privately in Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16:13); the men of Judah anointed him king over Judah at Hebron (2:4); now the elders of all Israel anoint him. What God promised in the first anointing comes about step by step.

decisions.choice: leaders; poured oil on his head to make him king
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", who were the senior heads of families and tribes, and explains what anointing is, as at 1 Samuel 9:16.

source.text: בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֛ה דָּוִ֖ד בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה מָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of thirty years [was] David when he became king; forty years he reigned.

en.L: David [was] a son of thirty years when he became king; he reigned forty years.
en.B: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and his reign lasted forty years.
en.R: David was thirty years old when he became king. He ruled for forty years.

es.L: Hijo de treinta años [era] David cuando comenzó a reinar; reinó cuarenta años.
es.B: David tenía treinta años cuando comenzó a reinar, y su reinado duró cuarenta años.
es.R: David tenía treinta años cuando llegó a ser rey. Gobernó durante cuarenta años.

fr.L: David [était] fils de trente ans quand il devint roi ; il régna quarante ans.
fr.B: David avait trente ans quand il commença à régner, et son règne dura quarante ans.
fr.R: David avait trente ans quand il est devenu roi. Il a régné pendant quarante ans.

vi.L: Đa-vít [được] ba mươi tuổi khi lên làm vua; ông trị vì bốn mươi năm.
vi.B: Đa-vít được ba mươi tuổi khi lên ngôi, và ông trị vì bốn mươi năm.
vi.R: Đa-vít được ba mươi tuổi khi lên làm vua. Ông cai trị bốn mươi năm.

decisions.choice: a son of thirty years: thirty years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years (Genesis 7:6; 1 Samuel 4:15).

decisions.choice: the opening formula of a king's reign
decisions.reason: The notice of a king's age when he began to reign and the length of his reign is the pattern the books of Samuel and Kings use for each king (1 Samuel 13:1; 2 Samuel 2:10; 1 Kings 14:21). Here it stands at the point where David becomes king of the whole nation. Forty is a round figure; verse 5 gives the exact years.

source.text: בְּחֶבְרוֹן֙ מָלַ֣ךְ עַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם מָלַ֗ךְ שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְשָׁלֹשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה עַ֥ל כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.

en.L: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
en.B: At Hebron he reigned over Judah for seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.
en.R: He ruled over Judah from Hebron for seven and a half years. Then he ruled over all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

es.L: En Hebrón reinó sobre Judá siete años y seis meses, y en Jerusalén reinó treinta y tres años sobre todo Israel y Judá.
es.B: En Hebrón reinó sobre Judá durante siete años y seis meses, y en Jerusalén reinó sobre todo Israel y Judá durante treinta y tres años.
es.R: Gobernó sobre Judá desde Hebrón durante siete años y medio. Después gobernó sobre todo Israel y Judá desde Jerusalén durante treinta y tres años.

fr.L: À Hébron, il régna sur Juda sept ans et six mois, et à Jérusalem il régna trente-trois ans sur tout Israël et Juda.
fr.B: À Hébron, il régna sur Juda pendant sept ans et six mois, et à Jérusalem il régna sur tout Israël et Juda pendant trente-trois ans.
fr.R: Il a régné sur Juda depuis Hébron pendant sept ans et demi. Ensuite, il a régné sur tout Israël et Juda depuis Jérusalem pendant trente-trois ans.

vi.L: Tại Hếp-rôn, ông trị vì Giu-đa bảy năm sáu tháng, và tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, ông trị vì ba mươi ba năm trên toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa.
vi.B: Tại Hếp-rôn, ông trị vì Giu-đa bảy năm sáu tháng, và tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, ông trị vì toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa ba mươi ba năm.
vi.R: Ông cai trị Giu-đa tại Hếp-rôn bảy năm rưỡi. Sau đó ông cai trị toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa tại Giê-ru-sa-lem ba mươi ba năm.

decisions.choice: seven and a half years plus thirty-three: forty and a half years in all
decisions.reason: The exact figures add up to forty years and six months, which verse 4 and 1 Kings 2:11 round to forty. The seven and a half years at Hebron are also given in 2:11.

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem: the summary looks ahead
decisions.reason: The verse names Jerusalem as David's capital before the story of how he took it (verses 6-9). It sums up the whole reign at its turning point.

decisions.choice: all Israel and Judah: two parts of the nation under one king
decisions.reason: The writer names Israel and Judah side by side, because they had stood apart under two kings (2:8-11) and would divide again after Solomon (1 Kings 12:16-20). David ruled both.

decisions.choice: seven and a half years
decisions.reason: Readable says "seven and a half years" for "seven years and six months"; the length is the same.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֶל־הַיְבֻסִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לְדָוִ֤ד לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־תָב֣וֹא הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֣י אִם־הֱסִֽירְךָ֗ הַעִוְרִ֤ים וְהַפִּסְחִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא דָוִ֖ד הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the king and his men [to] Jerusalem, against the Jebusite, dweller of the land; and it said to David, saying, Not you will come here, for rather will turn you aside the blind and the lame, saying, Not will come David here.

en.L: And the king and his men went [to] Jerusalem, against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land; and they said to David, "You will not come in here, but the blind and the lame will turn you away," saying, "David will not come in here."
en.B: Then the king and his men marched on Jerusalem, against the Jebusites who lived in that land. They told David, "You will not get in here; even the blind and the lame can fend you off." By this they meant, "David cannot get in here."
en.R: Then King David and his men went to attack Jerusalem. The Jebusites lived there, and they said to David, "You will never get inside this city! Even people who are blind or lame could keep you out!" They were sure that David could not get in.

es.L: Y fue el rey con sus hombres [a] Jerusalén, contra los jebuseos, los habitantes de la tierra; y ellos dijeron a David: «No entrarás aquí, sino que los ciegos y los cojos te rechazarán», diciendo: «No entrará David aquí».
es.B: Luego el rey y sus hombres marcharon contra Jerusalén, contra los jebuseos que vivían en aquella tierra. Ellos le dijeron a David: «No entrarás aquí; hasta los ciegos y los cojos pueden rechazarte». Con eso querían decir: «David no podrá entrar aquí».
es.R: Luego el rey David y sus hombres fueron a atacar Jerusalén. Allí vivían los jebuseos, y le dijeron a David: «¡Nunca entrarás en esta ciudad! ¡Hasta los ciegos y los cojos podrían mantenerte afuera!». Estaban seguros de que David no podría entrar.

fr.L: Et le roi et ses hommes allèrent [à] Jérusalem, contre les Jébusiens, les habitants du pays ; et ils dirent à David : « Tu n’entreras pas ici, mais les aveugles et les boiteux te repousseront », pour dire : « David n’entrera pas ici. »
fr.B: Puis le roi et ses hommes marchèrent sur Jérusalem, contre les Jébusiens qui habitaient ce pays. Ceux-ci dirent à David : « Tu n’entreras pas ici ; même les aveugles et les boiteux suffiront à te repousser. » Ils voulaient dire : « David ne peut pas entrer ici. »
fr.R: Ensuite le roi David et ses hommes sont allés attaquer Jérusalem. Les Jébusiens vivaient là, et ils ont dit à David : « Tu n’entreras jamais dans cette ville ! Même des aveugles et des boiteux pourraient t’en empêcher ! » Ils étaient sûrs que David ne pourrait pas entrer.

vi.L: Vua và người của ông đi [đến] Giê-ru-sa-lem, đánh người Giê-bu-sít, là dân cư trong xứ; họ nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không vào được đây, vì ngay cả người mù và người què cũng sẽ đẩy lui ngươi," nghĩa là: "Đa-vít sẽ không vào được đây."
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua và người của ông tiến đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem, đánh người Giê-bu-sít, là dân sống trong vùng ấy. Họ nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không vào được đây đâu; ngay cả người mù và người què cũng đẩy lui được ngươi." Ý họ là: "Đa-vít không thể vào được đây."
vi.R: Rồi vua Đa-vít và người của ông đi đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem. Người Giê-bu-sít sống ở đó nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không bao giờ vào được thành này! Ngay cả người mù hay người què cũng đủ sức chặn ngươi lại!" Họ chắc rằng Đa-vít không thể nào vào được.

decisions.choice: the Jebusites: the Canaanite people who still held Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jebusites are named among the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 15:21; Deuteronomy 7:1). Neither Judah nor Benjamin had been able to drive them out of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:63; Judges 1:21), and it was still a foreign town in the days of the judges (Judges 19:10-12). The Hebrew says "the Jebusite", one name standing for the whole people.

decisions.choice: but the blind and the lame will turn you away: a taunt that the city is too strong to take
alternatives: unless you remove the blind and the lame
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, and its consonants can be read in two ways: as "the blind and the lame will turn you away", or as "unless you remove the blind and the lame". The first reading is followed here. Either way the Jebusites are mocking David: their walls are so strong that even blind and lame defenders could hold them. The words become a saying in verse 8.

decisions.choice: saying, David will not come in here: what they meant by the taunt
decisions.reason: The second "saying" explains the Jebusites' words. Their boast amounts to the claim that David cannot enter the city.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 11:4-5 retells verses 6-7
decisions.reason: Chronicles says that David and all Israel went to "Jerusalem, that is, Jebus", and gives the Jebusites' boast as "You will not come in here", without the words about the blind and the lame.

decisions.choice: Even ... can fend you off. By this they meant (Balanced); Even people who are blind or lame could keep you out! They were sure (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the boast plain, and turn the second "saying" into a separate sentence that tells what the Jebusites meant.

decisions.choice: "người Giê-bu-sít"; the Jebusites call David "ngươi"
decisions.reason: The people's name as the Samuel terms note gives it; the taunt uses the contemptuous "ngươi".

source.text: וַיִּלְכֹּ֣ד דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֖ת מְצֻדַ֣ת צִיּ֑וֹן הִ֖יא עִ֥יר דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And captured David the stronghold of Zion; it [is] the city of David.

en.L: But David captured the stronghold of Zion; that [is] the City of David.
en.B: But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is now the City of David.
en.R: But David captured the fortress of Zion. It became known as the City of David.

es.L: Pero David tomó la fortaleza de Sion; esa [es] la ciudad de David.
es.B: Pero David tomó la fortaleza de Sion, que ahora es la ciudad de David.
es.R: Pero David conquistó la fortaleza de Sion. Llegó a conocerse como la ciudad de David.

fr.L: Mais David s’empara de la forteresse de Sion ; c’[est] la cité de David.
fr.B: Mais David s’empara de la forteresse de Sion, qui est aujourd’hui la cité de David.
fr.R: Mais David s’est emparé de la forteresse de Sion. On l’a appelée ensuite la cité de David.

vi.L: Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được đồn lũy Si-ôn; đó [là] thành Đa-vít.
vi.B: Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được đồn lũy Si-ôn, nay là thành Đa-vít.
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được pháo đài Si-ôn. Nơi ấy được gọi là thành Đa-vít.

decisions.choice: Zion: the fortified hill of the Jebusite city
decisions.reason: This is the first time Zion is named in the Bible. It was the ridge south of the later temple hill, on which the old city stood. In later books the name grows to mean the whole of Jerusalem, and the place where Yahweh dwells among his people (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 2:3).

decisions.choice: stronghold: a fortified height
decisions.reason: The word names a high place made strong for defense, like the strongholds where David hid from Saul (1 Samuel 22:4; 24:1). Here it is the walled citadel of the city.

decisions.choice: that is the City of David: a note from the writer's day
decisions.reason: The writer explains the old name by the one his readers knew. Verse 9 tells how the name was given. The capture itself is told in one short clause, in contrast to the Jebusites' long boast.

decisions.choice: which is now (Balanced); It became known as (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the name "City of David" came later, from David himself (verse 9). Readable says "fortress" for "stronghold", a more common word for a walled place.

decisions.choice: la forteresse de Sion; la cité de David
decisions.reason: "La cité de David" as the Samuel terms note sets; "forteresse" for the fortified height (m2) at every level, where the English moves from "stronghold" to "fortress".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא כָּל־מַכֵּ֤ה יְבֻסִי֙ וְיִגַּ֣ע בַּצִּנּ֔וֹר וְאֶת־הַפִּסְחִים֙ וְאֶת־הַ֣עִוְרִ֔ים שְׂנֻאֵ֖י נֶ֣פֶשׁ דָּוִ֑ד עַל־כֵּן֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ עִוֵּ֣ר וּפִסֵּ֔חַ לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא אֶל־הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David on the day that, Anyone striking a Jebusite, and let him reach by the water shaft, and the lame and the blind, hated of [the] soul of David — therefore they say, Blind and lame not will come into the house.

en.L: And David said on that day, "Whoever strikes a Jebusite, let him reach by the water shaft both the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul." Therefore they say, "The blind and the lame will not come into the house."
en.B: On that day David said, "Whoever would strike down the Jebusites must go up through the water shaft to reach the lame and the blind, whom David hates." That is why people say, "The blind and the lame will not come into the house."
en.R: That day David told his men, "Anyone who wants to defeat the Jebusites must climb up through the water tunnel to get at those blind and lame people that David hates." That is why people say, "The blind and the lame will not come into the house."

es.L: Y dijo David aquel día: «Cualquiera que hiera a un jebuseo, que llegue por el canal del agua a los cojos y a los ciegos, aborrecidos por el alma de David». Por eso dicen: «Ciego y cojo no entrarán en la casa».
es.B: Aquel día David dijo: «Quien quiera derrotar a los jebuseos tendrá que subir por el canal del agua para llegar a los cojos y a los ciegos, a quienes David aborrece». Por eso la gente dice: «Ni ciegos ni cojos entrarán en la casa».
es.R: Aquel día David les dijo a sus hombres: «Cualquiera que quiera vencer a los jebuseos tendrá que trepar por el túnel del agua para llegar a esos ciegos y cojos que David aborrece». Por eso la gente dice: «Ni ciegos ni cojos entrarán en la casa».

fr.L: Et David dit ce jour-là : « Quiconque frappe un Jébusien, qu’il atteigne par le canal les boiteux et les aveugles, qui sont haïs de l’âme de David. » C’est pourquoi on dit : « Aveugle et boiteux n’entreront pas dans la maison. »
fr.B: Ce jour-là, David déclara : « Quiconque veut abattre les Jébusiens doit monter par le canal pour atteindre ces boiteux et ces aveugles que David déteste. » C’est pourquoi l’on dit : « Aveugle et boiteux n’entreront pas dans la maison. »
fr.R: Ce jour-là, David a dit à ses hommes : « Celui qui veut battre les Jébusiens doit grimper par le tunnel de l’eau pour aller attaquer ces aveugles et ces boiteux que David déteste. » C’est pour cela qu’on dit : « Les aveugles et les boiteux n’entreront pas dans la maison. »

vi.L: Ngày ấy Đa-vít nói: "Ai muốn đánh người Giê-bu-sít, hãy theo đường dẫn nước mà đến với kẻ què và kẻ mù, là những kẻ linh hồn Đa-vít ghét." Vì thế người ta nói: "Kẻ mù và kẻ què sẽ không vào nhà."
vi.B: Ngày ấy Đa-vít nói: "Ai muốn đánh người Giê-bu-sít thì phải leo lên theo đường dẫn nước để đến với những kẻ què và kẻ mù mà Đa-vít ghét." Vì thế người ta có câu: "Kẻ mù và kẻ què sẽ không được vào nhà."
vi.R: Ngày ấy Đa-vít bảo người của mình: "Ai muốn đánh thắng người Giê-bu-sít thì phải leo lên qua đường hầm dẫn nước để đến chỗ những kẻ mù và kẻ què mà Đa-vít ghét." Vì thế người ta có câu: "Kẻ mù và kẻ què sẽ không được vào nhà."

decisions.choice: the water shaft: a channel or shaft that brought water into the city
decisions.reason: The word appears elsewhere only in Psalm 42:8, where it seems to mean a rushing channel of water. Here it is most often taken as a shaft or tunnel from the spring below the city walls, through which attackers could climb up into the city. Others take it as a drain or gutter, as a grappling hook, or even as the throat, a place to strike the defenders. The sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: whoever strikes a Jebusite, let him reach ... the lame and the blind: David's order, left unfinished
alternatives: whoever strikes a Jebusite and reaches the water shaft (will be rewarded)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence does not run smoothly; it seems to break off without saying what will happen to the man who does this. The sense followed here is that whoever means to attack the Jebusites should get into the city by the water shaft and reach its defenders. 1 Chronicles 11:6 gives the promise that seems to be missing: whoever strikes the Jebusites first will become chief and commander, and Joab did so.

decisions.choice: the lame and the blind, whom David hates: David turns the taunt back on the Jebusites
decisions.reason: David takes up the Jebusites' boast from verse 6 and calls the defenders themselves "the lame and the blind". "Hated by David's soul" means hated by David himself; the soul stands for the whole person. The words are about the enemy in the city, not about people who are disabled; David later shows kindness to the lame Mephibosheth (9:1-13).

decisions.choice: hated by David's soul
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters read "who hate David's soul"; the form marked to be read aloud is "who are hated by David's soul". The read-aloud form is followed here. Both describe the defenders as David's enemies.

decisions.choice: the blind and the lame will not come into the house: a saying that grew from this event
decisions.reason: The writer explains a saying known in his own day. "The house" may be the house of the LORD, as the old Greek translation reads, since priests who were blind or lame could not serve at the altar (Leviticus 21:17-23); or it may be the palace, or a house in general. It is not clear which is meant.

decisions.choice: must go up through ... to reach (Balanced); must climb up through ... to get at (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give David's broken sentence a complete form, following the sense in m2. Readable says "water tunnel" and adds "his men" as the hearers.

decisions.choice: "đường dẫn nước" (L, B); "đường hầm dẫn nước" (R)
decisions.reason: A channel or shaft bringing water into the city (meaning decision); the word is uncertain, and Vietnamese keeps it general.

source.text: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב דָּוִד֙ בַּמְּצֻדָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָא־לָ֖הּ עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּ֤בֶן דָּוִד֙ סָבִ֔יב מִן־הַמִּלּ֖וֹא וָבָֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt David in the stronghold, and called it [the] city of David; and built David all around from the Millo and inward.

en.L: And David lived in the stronghold and called it the City of David. And David built all around, from the Millo and inward.
en.B: David took up residence in the stronghold and named it the City of David. He built up the area all around it, from the Millo inward.
en.R: David made his home in the fortress and named it the City of David. He built up the city all around it, from the Millo (a supporting terrace) inward.

es.L: Y habitó David en la fortaleza y la llamó la ciudad de David. Y edificó David alrededor, desde el Milo hacia adentro.
es.B: David se estableció en la fortaleza y la llamó la ciudad de David. Construyó en toda la zona de alrededor, desde el Milo hacia adentro.
es.R: David se fue a vivir a la fortaleza y la llamó la ciudad de David. Construyó toda la ciudad a su alrededor, desde el Milo (una terraza de apoyo) hacia adentro.

fr.L: Et David habita dans la forteresse et l’appela la cité de David. Et David bâtit tout autour, depuis le Millo et vers l’intérieur.
fr.B: David s’installa dans la forteresse et la nomma cité de David. Il construisit tout autour, depuis le Millo jusque vers l’intérieur.
fr.R: David s’est installé dans la forteresse et il l’a appelée la cité de David. Il a construit la ville tout autour, depuis le Millo (une grande terrasse de soutien) jusque vers l’intérieur.

vi.L: Đa-vít ở trong đồn lũy và gọi nơi ấy là thành Đa-vít. Đa-vít xây cất chung quanh, từ Mi-lô vào bên trong.
vi.B: Đa-vít ở trong đồn lũy và đặt tên là thành Đa-vít. Ông xây cất khu vực chung quanh, từ Mi-lô trở vào trong.
vi.R: Đa-vít ở trong pháo đài và đặt tên là thành Đa-vít. Ông xây dựng thành chung quanh đó, từ Mi-lô (một nền đất đắp cao) trở vào trong.

decisions.choice: the Millo: probably a terrace of built-up earth and stone
decisions.reason: The name comes from the verb "to fill", so it probably means a "filling": a great terrace or rampart of packed earth and stone that held up buildings on the steep slope of the hill. Solomon later rebuilt it (1 Kings 9:15, 24; 11:27). Its exact form and place are not known.

decisions.choice: called it the City of David: the king's own city
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lay on the border of Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8; 18:16) and had belonged to neither tribe. Taken by David and his own men, it became his city, a capital that no single tribe could claim.

decisions.choice: and inward: toward the inner part of the city
decisions.reason: The word means "to the house" or "inside". David built from the Millo on the outer edge toward the center, filling in the area around the stronghold.

decisions.choice: built up the area all around it (Balanced); built up the city all around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say what David built. Balanced and Readable supply the area around the stronghold, and Readable explains the Millo briefly.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד הָל֣וֹךְ וְגָד֑וֹל וַיהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went David going and great, and Yahweh, God of hosts, [was] with him.

en.L: And David went on becoming greater and greater, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts, [was] with him.
en.B: David became greater and greater, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, was with him.
en.R: David became more and more powerful, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, was with him.

es.L: Y David iba engrandeciéndose más y más, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los ejércitos, [estaba] con él.
es.B: David se hacía cada vez más grande, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los Ejércitos, estaba con él.
es.R: David se hacía cada vez más poderoso, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de los Ejércitos, estaba con él.

fr.L: Et David allait en grandissant de plus en plus, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, [était] avec lui.
fr.B: David devint de plus en plus grand, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, était avec lui.
fr.R: David est devenu de plus en plus puissant, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu des armées, était avec lui.

vi.L: Đa-vít càng ngày càng lớn mạnh, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, ở với ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít ngày càng hùng mạnh, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, ở với ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít ngày càng hùng mạnh, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân, ở với ông.

decisions.choice: went going and great: grew steadily greater
decisions.reason: The verb "go" with a second verb describes something that keeps on happening (Genesis 26:13; 1 Samuel 2:26). David's power and fame kept growing.

decisions.choice: Yahweh, the God of hosts: Yahweh, commander of the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: This fuller form of the title adds "God". Its meaning is explained at 1 Samuel 1:3.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was with him: the reason for David's rise
decisions.reason: The same words run through David's story (1 Samuel 16:18; 18:12, 14, 28). His success comes from God's presence, not from his own skill alone. The "and" joining the two clauses gives the reason for the first.

decisions.choice: for, because; the God of Armies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the second clause gives the reason. They say "Armies" for "hosts", as at 1 Samuel 1:3.

decisions.choice: le Dieu des armées (every level)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets "le SEIGNEUR des armées" for *YHWH tseba'ot*: French "armées" already says what the English Balanced and Readable "Armies" say, so the title is the same at every level.

decisions.choice: "el Dios de los ejércitos" (L); "el Dios de los Ejércitos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for tseba'ot ("el SEÑOR de los ejércitos" at Literal, "de los Ejércitos" at Balanced and Readable), here with "Dios" as the Hebrew has.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời Vạn Quân" at every level
alternatives: "Đức Chúa Trời của các đạo binh"
decisions.reason: As the Psalms and Samuel terms notes set for "the LORD of hosts": "Vạn Quân" is the Vietnamese title for the God who commands the armies of heaven and earth (meaning decision), used at every level where the English says "hosts" or "Armies".

source.text: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צֹ֥ר מַלְאָכִים֮ אֶל־דָּוִד֒ וַעֲצֵ֣י אֲרָזִ֔ים וְחָרָשֵׁ֣י עֵ֔ץ וְחָֽרָשֵׁ֖י אֶ֣בֶן קִ֑יר וַיִּבְנֽוּ־בַ֖יִת לְדָוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Hiram king of Tyre messengers to David, and trees of cedars, and craftsmen of wood and craftsmen of stone of wall; and they built a house for David.

en.L: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and craftsmen of wood and craftsmen of wall stone; and they built a house for David.
en.B: Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, with cedar logs, woodworkers and stonemasons, and they built David a palace.
en.R: Hiram, the king of Tyre, sent messengers to David. He also sent cedar logs and workers skilled with wood and stone, and they built a palace for David.

es.L: Y Hiram rey de Tiro envió mensajeros a David, y madera de cedro, y artesanos de la madera y artesanos de la piedra de muro; y edificaron una casa para David.
es.B: Hiram, rey de Tiro, envió embajadores a David, con troncos de cedro, carpinteros y canteros, y le construyeron a David un palacio.
es.R: Hiram, el rey de Tiro, envió mensajeros a David. También le mandó troncos de cedro y trabajadores expertos en madera y en piedra, y construyeron un palacio para David.

fr.L: Et Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya à David des messagers, et des bois de cèdre, et des artisans du bois et des artisans de la pierre de mur ; et ils bâtirent une maison pour David.
fr.B: Hiram, roi de Tyr, envoya des messagers à David, avec du bois de cèdre, des charpentiers et des tailleurs de pierre, et ils bâtirent un palais pour David.
fr.R: Hiram, le roi de Tyr, a envoyé des messagers à David. Il a aussi envoyé du bois de cèdre et des ouvriers habiles à travailler le bois et la pierre, et ils ont construit un palais pour David.

vi.L: Hi-ram vua Ty-rơ sai sứ giả đến cùng Đa-vít, cùng với gỗ bá hương, thợ mộc và thợ đá xây tường; họ xây cho Đa-vít một cung điện.
vi.B: Hi-ram vua Ty-rơ sai sứ giả đến cùng Đa-vít, mang theo gỗ bá hương, thợ mộc và thợ đá, và họ xây cho Đa-vít một cung điện.
vi.R: Hi-ram, vua thành Ty-rơ, sai sứ giả đến gặp Đa-vít. Vua cũng gửi gỗ bá hương cùng những người thợ giỏi nghề mộc và nghề đá đến, và họ xây cho Đa-vít một cung điện.

decisions.choice: Hiram king of Tyre: ruler of a rich trading city on the coast north of Israel
decisions.reason: Tyre was a Phoenician port, famous for its trade and its builders. Cedar grew in the mountains of Lebanon behind it and was the finest building timber of the region. The same king later supplied Solomon with cedar and workers for the temple (1 Kings 5:15-25). The writer groups David's building with his other successes here; the visit may have come later in his reign.

decisions.choice: a house: a palace
decisions.reason: The word "house" is used for any dwelling, from a tent to a royal palace. Built of cedar by skilled workers, this is David's palace, the "house of cedar" he speaks of in 7:2.

decisions.choice: craftsmen of wood and of wall stone: carpenters and masons
decisions.reason: "Stone of wall" is stone cut and shaped for building walls. Hiram sends skilled workers of both kinds, which Israel at this time seems to have lacked.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 14:1-2 retells verses 11-12
decisions.reason: The Chronicles account is almost the same, with "to build him a house" in place of "and they built a house for David", and "his kingdom was lifted high" put more strongly.

decisions.choice: woodworkers and stonemasons (Balanced); workers skilled with wood and stone (Readable); palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words for these trades, and call the king's house a palace.

decisions.choice: "cung điện" at every level for "a house"
decisions.reason: A king's house is a palace (meaning decision); Vietnamese "nhà" for a king would sound too small, so Literal also says "cung điện".

records.literal_gloss: And knew David that had established him Yahweh as king over Israel, and that was lifted up his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

en.L: And David knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had established him as king over Israel, and that his kingdom was lifted up for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.B: Then David knew that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made him secure as king over Israel, and had raised his kingdom high for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.
en.R: Then David understood that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made him king over Israel and made his kingdom great. He did it for the good of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel.

es.L: Y supo David que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había establecido como rey sobre Israel, y que su reino había sido enaltecido por amor a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.
es.B: Entonces David supo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había afirmado como rey sobre Israel, y que había engrandecido su reino por amor a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.
es.R: Entonces David comprendió que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había hecho rey de Israel y había engrandecido su reino. Lo hizo por el bien de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel.

fr.L: Et David sut que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait affermi comme roi sur Israël, et que son royaume était élevé à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.
fr.B: David reconnut alors que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait établi solidement comme roi sur Israël et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait élevé son royaume à cause de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.
fr.R: Alors David a compris que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait fait roi sur Israël et qu’il avait rendu son royaume puissant. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait fait pour le bien de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple Israël.

vi.L: Đa-vít biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững ông làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, và đã tôn cao vương quốc ông vì cớ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít biết rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập vững ngôi vua của ông trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, và đã làm cho vương quốc ông được hưng thịnh vì cớ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Đa-vít hiểu rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lập ông làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên và làm cho vương quốc ông lớn mạnh. Ngài làm vậy vì lợi ích của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: had established him: had set him firmly in place as king
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or secure. It is the word Yahweh will use in his promise to David that his kingdom will be established forever (7:12-16).

decisions.choice: for the sake of his people Israel: Yahweh's people
decisions.reason: "His people" is best taken as Yahweh's people, as in verse 2 ("my people Israel"). David understands that he has been made great not for himself but for the good of the nation that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: was lifted up: made great by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, but the sentence makes clear who did the lifting: the same Yahweh who established David as king.

decisions.choice: had raised his kingdom high (Balanced); made his kingdom great. He did it for the good of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive verb into an active one with Yahweh as subject, as m3 explains. Readable splits the sentence in two.

decisions.choice: Le SEIGNEUR l'avait fait (R)
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable starts a new sentence with "He", French repeats the divine name so that the subject is plain after a sentence about David.

records.literal_gloss: And took David more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after his coming from Hebron, and were born more to David sons and daughters.

en.L: And David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
en.B: David took further concubines and wives from Jerusalem after he left Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
en.R: After David moved from Hebron to Jerusalem, he took more wives and concubines (secondary wives) from among the people of Jerusalem. He had more sons and daughters.

es.L: Y tomó David más concubinas y mujeres de Jerusalén después de venir de Hebrón, y le nacieron a David más hijos e hijas.
es.B: David tomó más concubinas y esposas de Jerusalén después de dejar Hebrón, y le nacieron más hijos e hijas.
es.R: Después de mudarse de Hebrón a Jerusalén, David tomó más esposas y concubinas (esposas de segundo rango) de entre la gente de Jerusalén. Tuvo más hijos e hijas.

fr.L: Et David prit encore des concubines et des femmes de Jérusalem, après être venu d’Hébron, et il naquit encore à David des fils et des filles.
fr.B: David prit encore des concubines et des femmes de Jérusalem après son départ d’Hébron, et il lui naquit encore des fils et des filles.
fr.R: Quand David est parti d’Hébron pour s’installer à Jérusalem, il a pris d’autres femmes et d’autres concubines (des épouses de second rang) parmi les habitants de Jérusalem. Il a eu encore des fils et des filles.

vi.L: Sau khi từ Hếp-rôn đến, Đa-vít lấy thêm vợ lẽ và vợ từ Giê-ru-sa-lem, và Đa-vít sinh thêm con trai con gái.
vi.B: Sau khi rời Hếp-rôn, Đa-vít lấy thêm vợ lẽ và vợ ở Giê-ru-sa-lem, và ông có thêm con trai con gái.
vi.R: Sau khi từ Hếp-rôn dời về Giê-ru-sa-lem, Đa-vít lấy thêm vợ và vợ lẽ, tức là vợ thứ, trong số người Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ông có thêm nhiều con trai con gái.

decisions.choice: concubines and wives: wives of full and of lower standing
decisions.reason: A concubine was a lawful wife of lower rank, without the full rights of a chief wife. Many wives were a sign of a king's power and wealth, and some marriages sealed alliances (3:3). The law warned a king not to take many wives (Deuteronomy 17:17).

decisions.choice: from Jerusalem: women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The women came from the city, now his capital; the words may also simply mean "in Jerusalem". 1 Chronicles 14:3 has "in Jerusalem".

decisions.choice: more: added to the sons born at Hebron
decisions.reason: The word "more" looks back to the six sons born to David at Hebron (3:2-5).

decisions.choice: concubines (secondary wives)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "concubine" the first time it appears in the chapter, as in Judges.

decisions.choice: "vợ lẽ" (L, B); "vợ lẽ, tức là vợ thứ" (R)
decisions.reason: A wife of lower standing (meaning decision); "vợ lẽ" is the plain Vietnamese word, and Readable explains it as the English does.

decisions.choice: Nathan and Solomon: sons through whom David's line continued
decisions.reason: Solomon succeeded David as king (1 Kings 1:39); Nathan is named in the line of Jesus in Luke 3:31. 1 Chronicles 3:5 says that these four were the sons of Bathsheba, whose story is told in chapters 11-12. The list is placed here because it belongs with David's household in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the list of sons appears also in 1 Chronicles 3:5-8 and 14:4-7
decisions.reason: Both lists in Chronicles name thirteen sons born in Jerusalem, where this list has eleven: they add Elpelet (or Eliphelet) and Nogah. Chronicles 3:5 spells Shammua as Shimea.

decisions.choice: the children (Balanced); the sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "those born". Every name in the list is a son's, so Readable says "sons"; daughters are mentioned in verse 13 but not named.

decisions.choice: "los hijos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" takes in sons and children alike, so Balanced and Readable can say the same word for the English "children" and "sons".

decisions.choice: "Sam-mua", "Sô-báp", and verses 15-16 "Gi-ba", "Ê-li-sua", "Nê-phéc", "Gia-phia", "Ê-li-sa-ma", "Ê-li-a-đa", "Ê-li-phê-lết"
decisions.reason: Names not in the terms note's table, given the usual Protestant forms; Nathan and Solomon as the table.

decisions.choice: Eliada: called Beeliada in 1 Chronicles 14:7
decisions.reason: The names mean "God knows" (Eliada) and "the Lord knows" (Beeliada), where "lord" is the word baal. When Baal came to stand for the Canaanite god, names with it were often rewritten with "God" (El) in its place, as here.

records.literal_gloss: And heard Philistines that they had anointed David as king over Israel, and went up all Philistines to seek David; and heard David and went down to the stronghold.

en.L: And the Philistines heard that they had anointed David [as] king over Israel, and all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard [of it] and went down to the stronghold.
en.B: News reached the Philistines that David had been anointed king over Israel, so the whole Philistine force went up to hunt for him. But David heard of it and went down to the stronghold.
en.R: The Philistines heard that David had been made king over Israel. So their whole army came up to search for him. But David heard about it and went down to the stronghold.

es.L: Y oyeron los filisteos que habían ungido a David [como] rey sobre Israel, y subieron todos los filisteos a buscar a David; y David lo oyó y descendió a la fortaleza.
es.B: Llegó a oídos de los filisteos que David había sido ungido rey sobre Israel, así que todas las fuerzas filisteas subieron a buscarlo. Pero David se enteró y bajó a la fortaleza.
es.R: Los filisteos oyeron que David había sido hecho rey de Israel. Así que todo su ejército subió a buscarlo. Pero David se enteró y bajó a la fortaleza.

fr.L: Et les Philistins apprirent qu’on avait oint David [comme] roi sur Israël, et tous les Philistins montèrent pour chercher David ; et David [l’]apprit et descendit à la forteresse.
fr.B: Les Philistins apprirent que David avait été oint comme roi sur Israël, et toutes leurs forces montèrent pour le traquer. Mais David l’apprit et descendit à la forteresse.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont appris qu’on avait fait de David le roi d’Israël. Alors toute leur armée est montée pour le chercher. Mais David l’a appris et il est descendu à la forteresse.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin nghe rằng người ta đã xức dầu cho Đa-vít làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, thì toàn thể người Phi-li-tin kéo lên để tìm Đa-vít; Đa-vít nghe [vậy] liền đi xuống đồn lũy.
vi.B: Khi người Phi-li-tin nghe tin Đa-vít đã được xức dầu làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, toàn quân Phi-li-tin kéo lên truy tìm ông. Nhưng Đa-vít nghe biết và đi xuống đồn lũy.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin nghe tin Đa-vít đã được lập làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vì vậy toàn quân của họ kéo lên để lùng bắt ông. Nhưng Đa-vít biết được và đi xuống đồn lũy.

decisions.choice: the Philistines heard: a united Israel under David was now a threat to them
decisions.reason: The Philistines had held power over much of Israel since Saul's defeat (1 Samuel 31:7). David had once lived among them as a vassal of the king of Gath (1 Samuel 27:1-7), and they seem to have left him alone while he ruled Judah only. A king over all Israel was another matter.

decisions.choice: to seek David: to hunt him down
decisions.reason: To "seek" a person is often to look for him in order to kill him, as Saul sought David (1 Samuel 23:14; 24:3). The whole Philistine army sets out against him.

decisions.choice: went down to the stronghold: probably a fortified place in the hills of Judah, not the stronghold of Zion
decisions.reason: David "went down", so this stronghold seems to lie lower than Jerusalem, perhaps Adullam, where he had hidden before (1 Samuel 22:1-5; 2 Samuel 23:13-14). If so, the battles of verses 17-25 may have come before the capture of Jerusalem in verses 6-9, and the writer has arranged the events by subject. It is also possible that the stronghold of Zion is meant.

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 14:8-17 retells verses 17-25
decisions.reason: Chronicles follows this account closely. In this verse it says that David "went out against them" in place of "went down to the stronghold".

decisions.choice: the whole Philistine force (Balanced); their whole army (Readable)
decisions.reason: "All the Philistines" means their full fighting force, so Balanced and Readable say so.

en.B: Now the Philistines had come and spread out across the Valley of Rephaim.
en.R: The Philistines came and spread out over the Valley of Rephaim.

es.R: Los filisteos llegaron y se extendieron por todo el valle de Refaím.

fr.B: Les Philistins étaient arrivés et s’étaient répandus dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.R: Les Philistins sont arrivés et ils se sont répandus dans la vallée des Rephaïm.

vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin kéo đến và tràn ra khắp thung lũng Rê-pha-im.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Rephaim: a broad valley just southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The valley lay on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8; 18:16) and was a natural route from the Philistine plain up into the hills. The name recalls the Rephaim, an ancient people known for their size (Deuteronomy 2:11, 20).

decisions.choice: spread out: deployed across the valley, raiding
decisions.reason: The verb is used of raiders spread over a land (Judges 15:9; 1 Samuel 30:16). The Philistines occupy the valley close to the heart of David's land.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶֽעֱלֶה֙ אֶל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הֲתִתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיָדִ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־דָּוִד֙ עֲלֵ֔ה כִּֽי־נָתֹ֥ן אֶתֵּ֛ן אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I go up against Philistines? Will you give them into my hand? And said Yahweh to David, Go up, for surely I will give the Philistines into your hand.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I go up against [the] Philistines? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them into my hand?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to David, "Go up, for I will surely give the Philistines into your hand."
en.B: So David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Am I to go up against the Philistines? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hand them over to me?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered David, "Go up, for I will certainly hand the Philistines over to you."
en.R: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go and attack the Philistines? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me victory over them?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered David, "Go and attack them. I will certainly give you victory over the Philistines."

es.L: Y consultó David {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Subiré contra los filisteos? ¿Los entregarás en mi mano?». Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a David: «Sube, porque ciertamente entregaré a los filisteos en tu mano».
es.B: Entonces David consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo subir contra los filisteos? ¿Me los entregarás?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió a David: «Sube, porque de seguro te entregaré a los filisteos».
es.R: David le preguntó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo ir a atacar a los filisteos? ¿Me darás la victoria sobre ellos?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió a David: «Ve y atácalos. Sin duda te daré la victoria sobre los filisteos».

fr.L: Et David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Monterai-je contre [les] Philistins ? Les livreras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entre mes mains ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à David : « Monte, car je livrerai certainement les Philistins entre tes mains. »
fr.B: David consulta donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Dois-je monter contre les Philistins ? Me les livreras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit à David : « Monte, car je vais assurément te livrer les Philistins. »
fr.R: David a demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Est-ce que je dois aller attaquer les Philistins ? Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas me donner la victoire sur eux ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu à David : « Va les attaquer. Je vais certainement te donner la victoire sur les Philistins. »

vi.L: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Con có nên đi lên đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có trao chúng vào tay con không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Đa-vít: "Hãy đi lên, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn sẽ trao người Phi-li-tin vào tay con."
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đi lên đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có trao chúng vào tay con không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Đa-vít: "Hãy đi lên, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn sẽ trao người Phi-li-tin vào tay con."
vi.R: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đi đánh người Phi-li-tin không? Ngài có cho con thắng họ không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Đa-vít: "Hãy đi đánh chúng. Ta chắc chắn sẽ cho con thắng người Phi-li-tin."

decisions.choice: inquired of Yahweh: asked God for an answer, probably through the priest
decisions.reason: As at 1 Samuel 23:2 and 30:7-8, David seeks Yahweh's guidance before battle, likely through the priest Abiathar and the ephod, which gave answers to questions like these.

decisions.choice: give into my hand: give me power over them, victory
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. To give an enemy into someone's hand is to grant victory over him.

decisions.choice: I will surely give: a strong promise
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in the Hebrew ("giving I will give") to stress certainty.

decisions.choice: asked; attack; give victory over
decisions.reason: Readable says "asked" for "inquired of", says "attack" for "go up against", and explains the idiom "give into the hand", as at 1 Samuel 23:2-4.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span on "¿Los entregarás?"
alternatives: "¿Tú los entregarás?", with a span on "tú"
decisions.reason: For the whole of 2 Samuel, as in the Spanish Pentateuch: the deity pronoun setting goes only on the words for God that Spanish writes out (él, lo, le, su, tú, te, ti, tu, mi, me); where the English "you" or "he" is only in the Spanish verb ending, as here, there is no span.

decisions.choice: "Ta" in a deity_pronoun span where God speaks of himself
decisions.reason: The English has no span on God's "I"; Vietnamese marks God's "Ta" mid-sentence, as the Genesis note sets.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א דָוִ֥ד בְּבַֽעַל־פְּרָצִים֮ וַיַּכֵּ֣ם שָׁ֣ם דָּוִד֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר פָּרַ֨ץ יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־אֹיְבַ֛י לְפָנַ֖י כְּפֶ֣רֶץ מָ֑יִם עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּ֥עַל פְּרָצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And came David to Baal-perazim and struck them there David, and said, Has broken through Yahweh my enemies before me like a breaking through of waters; therefore he called [the] name of the place that Baal-perazim.

en.L: And David came to Baal-perazim, and David struck them there, and he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has broken through my enemies before me like a breaking through of waters." Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
en.B: So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated them there. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has burst through my enemies ahead of me, like water breaking through." That is why that place was named Baal-perazim.
en.R: So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated the Philistines there. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} broke through my enemies in front of me, the way a flood breaks through." That is why the place was called Baal-perazim, which means "Master of breaking through."

es.L: Y llegó David a Baal-perazim, y allí los hirió David, y dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha abierto brecha entre mis enemigos delante de mí como una brecha de aguas». Por eso llamó el nombre de aquel lugar Baal-perazim.
es.B: Así que David fue a Baal-perazim y allí los derrotó. Dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha irrumpido entre mis enemigos delante de mí, como el agua que rompe un dique». Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Baal-perazim.
es.R: Así que David fue a Baal-perazim y allí derrotó a los filisteos. Dijo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se abrió paso entre mis enemigos delante de mí, como una inundación que lo arrasa todo». Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Baal-perazim, que significa «Señor de las brechas».

fr.L: Et David vint à Baal-Peratsim, et David les frappa là, et il dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait une brèche dans mes ennemis devant moi comme une brèche que font les eaux. » C’est pourquoi il appela ce lieu du nom de Baal-Peratsim.
fr.B: David arriva donc à Baal-Peratsim et les battit là. Il dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a percé les rangs de mes ennemis devant moi, comme l’eau qui fait irruption. » C’est pourquoi on donna à ce lieu le nom de Baal-Peratsim.
fr.R: Alors David est allé à Baal-Peratsim et il a battu les Philistins. Il a dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a enfoncé mes ennemis devant moi, comme une inondation qui emporte tout. » C’est pourquoi on a appelé cet endroit Baal-Peratsim, ce qui veut dire « Maître des percées ».

vi.L: Đa-vít đến Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, và Đa-vít đánh bại chúng tại đó, và nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phá vỡ kẻ thù tôi trước mặt tôi như nước phá vỡ bờ." Vì thế ông gọi tên nơi ấy là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít đến Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim và đánh bại chúng tại đó. Ông nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phá tan kẻ thù trước mặt tôi như nước lũ vỡ bờ." Vì thế nơi ấy được gọi là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít đến Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim và đánh bại người Phi-li-tin tại đó. Ông nói: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phá tan kẻ thù trước mặt tôi như dòng nước lũ phá vỡ bờ đê." Vì thế nơi ấy được gọi là Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, nghĩa là "Chủ Phá Vỡ".

decisions.choice: like a breaking through of waters: like a flood bursting its banks
decisions.reason: The picture is of water that breaks out suddenly and sweeps everything before it. Yahweh scattered the Philistines in front of David as swiftly as that.

decisions.choice: Baal-perazim: "master of breakings through"
decisions.reason: Baal means "lord", "master" or "owner", and perazim comes from the verb "break through" in David's words. The name ties the place to what Yahweh did there. It is not certain whether "baal" here points to Yahweh as master, or whether the place already bore a name linked with the Canaanite god Baal and David's words give it a new meaning.

decisions.choice: Mount Perazim: recalled in Isaiah 28:21
decisions.reason: Isaiah warns that Yahweh will rise up "as at Mount Perazim", but this time against his own people. The same verb "break through" is used of Yahweh's anger against Uzzah in 6:8 (Perez-uzzah).

decisions.choice: That is why that place was named (Balanced); which means "Master of breaking through" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he called" has no clear subject other than David; Balanced and Readable use the passive. Readable explains the meaning of the name so that the reader sees the wordplay.

decisions.choice: "Ba-anh Phê-ra-xim, nghĩa là 'Chủ Phá Vỡ'"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name, as the English does; "baal" here means master, and "Chủ" keeps it apart from "Chúa", which this translation keeps for the Lord.

records.literal_gloss: And they abandoned there their idols, and carried them away David and his men.

en.L: And they abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
en.B: The Philistines left their idols behind there, and David and his men carried them off.
en.R: The Philistines ran away and left their idols behind, and David and his men took them away.

es.L: Y abandonaron allí sus ídolos, y David y sus hombres se los llevaron.
es.B: Los filisteos dejaron allí sus ídolos, y David y sus hombres se los llevaron.
es.R: Los filisteos huyeron y dejaron atrás sus ídolos, y David y sus hombres se los llevaron.

fr.L: Et ils abandonnèrent là leurs idoles, et David et ses hommes les emportèrent.
fr.B: Les Philistins laissèrent là leurs idoles, et David et ses hommes les emportèrent.
fr.R: Les Philistins se sont enfuis en laissant derrière eux leurs idoles, et David et ses hommes les ont emportées.

vi.L: Chúng bỏ lại các thần tượng của chúng tại đó, và Đa-vít cùng người của ông mang chúng đi.
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin bỏ lại các thần tượng của họ tại đó, và Đa-vít cùng người của ông mang chúng đi.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin chạy trốn, bỏ lại các thần tượng của họ. Đa-vít và người của ông mang các tượng ấy đi.

decisions.choice: their idols: images of their gods, brought to battle for protection
decisions.reason: Armies carried images of their gods into battle, as Israel once carried the ark (1 Samuel 4:3-11). There the Philistines captured the ark; here they flee and leave their gods behind, and David's men carry them away as plunder.

decisions.choice: carried them away: 1 Chronicles 14:12 says the idols were burned
decisions.reason: Chronicles reports that David gave orders and the idols were burned with fire, as the law commanded (Deuteronomy 7:5, 25). The two accounts may describe two steps: the idols were taken, then destroyed.

decisions.choice: The Philistines (Balanced, Readable); ran away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Philistines as the subject. Readable adds "ran away", since leaving their gods behind shows that they fled.

source.text: וַיֹּסִ֥פוּ ע֛וֹד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים לַֽעֲל֑וֹת וַיִּנָּֽטְשׁ֖וּ בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And added again Philistines to go up, and spread out in [the] valley of Rephaim.

en.L: And [the] Philistines came up yet again and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
en.B: Once again the Philistines came up and spread out across the Valley of Rephaim.
en.R: Later the Philistines came back again and spread out over the Valley of Rephaim.

es.L: Y volvieron otra vez los filisteos a subir, y se extendieron por el valle de Refaím.
es.B: Una vez más los filisteos subieron y se desplegaron por el valle de Refaím.
es.R: Más tarde los filisteos volvieron y se extendieron por todo el valle de Refaím.

fr.L: Et [les] Philistins montèrent encore une fois et se déployèrent dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.B: Une fois encore, les Philistins montèrent et se répandirent dans la vallée des Rephaïm.
fr.R: Plus tard, les Philistins sont revenus et ils se sont répandus encore dans la vallée des Rephaïm.

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin lại kéo lên lần nữa và tràn ra trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.B: Một lần nữa người Phi-li-tin kéo lên và dàn quân khắp thung lũng Rê-pha-im.
vi.R: Sau đó người Phi-li-tin lại kéo đến và tràn ra khắp thung lũng Rê-pha-im.

decisions.choice: added again to go up: a second attack
decisions.reason: The verb "add" with another verb means to do something again. The Philistines return to the same valley as in verse 18, and the second battle is told with the same words, so that the different answer from Yahweh in verse 23 stands out.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל דָּוִד֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֣א תַעֲלֶ֑ה הָסֵב֙ אֶל־אַ֣חֲרֵיהֶ֔ם וּבָ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם מִמּ֥וּל בְּכָאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, and he said, Not you will go up; go around to behind them, and come to them from in front of [the] balsam trees.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "You shall not go up; go around behind them and come upon them in front of the balsam trees.
en.B: When David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered, "Do not go straight up. Go around to their rear and attack them opposite the balsam trees.
en.R: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again what to do, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered, "Do not attack them from the front. Go around behind them and attack them near the balsam trees.

es.L: Y consultó David {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: «No subirás; rodéalos por detrás y ven contra ellos frente a los árboles de bálsamo.
es.B: Cuando David consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le respondió: «No subas de frente. Rodéalos por la retaguardia y atácalos frente a los árboles de bálsamo.
es.R: David volvió a preguntarle {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} qué debía hacer, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le respondió: «No los ataques de frente. Rodéalos y atácalos por detrás, cerca de los árboles de bálsamo.

fr.L: Et David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Tu ne monteras pas ; contourne-les par derrière, et arrive sur eux en face des baumiers.
fr.B: Quand David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit : « Ne monte pas droit sur eux. Contourne-les par l’arrière et attaque-les du côté des baumiers.
fr.R: David a de nouveau demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ce qu’il devait faire, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a répondu : « Ne les attaque pas de face. Fais le tour pour arriver derrière eux, et attaque-les près des baumiers.

vi.L: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Con chớ đi lên; hãy đi vòng ra phía sau chúng và đến đánh chúng ở phía trước những cây bóp-ca.
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp: "Đừng tấn công thẳng lên. Hãy đi vòng ra phía sau chúng và đánh chúng ở phía đối diện những cây bóp-ca.
vi.R: Đa-vít lại cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nên làm gì, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp: "Đừng tấn công chúng từ phía trước. Hãy đi vòng ra phía sau chúng và tấn công gần những cây bóp-ca.

decisions.choice: balsam trees: a kind of tree, not certainly known
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, in verse 24, and in the parallel 1 Chronicles 14:14-15. It may name the balsam, a shrub that gives a gum, or another tree such as the mulberry or poplar. The name may be linked with the verb "weep", from the drops of sap some trees give.

decisions.choice: you shall not go up; go around: a different plan from the first battle
decisions.reason: The first time Yahweh said "Go up" (verse 19); now he forbids a direct attack and sends David around to take the Philistines from behind. Victory comes by obeying each new word, not by repeating what worked before.

decisions.choice: Do not go straight up (Balanced); Do not attack them from the front (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that only a head-on attack is forbidden; David is still to fight.

decisions.choice: les baumiers
decisions.reason: The tree is not certainly known (m1). French "baumier" is the balsam tree, as the English says; "mûrier", the older French rendering, is one guess among others.

decisions.choice: "cây bóp-ca"
decisions.reason: The tree is not certainly known (meaning decision); Vietnamese transliterates the Hebrew name, as the English "balsam" is only a guess.

source.text: וִ֠יהִי כְּֽשָׁמְעֲךָ֞ אֶת־ק֧וֹל צְעָדָ֛ה בְּרָאשֵׁ֥י הַבְּכָאִ֖ים אָ֣ז תֶּחֱרָ֑ץ כִּ֣י אָ֗ז יָצָ֤א יְהוָה֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לְהַכּ֖וֹת בְּמַחֲנֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And let it be, when you hear [the] sound of marching in [the] tops of the balsam trees, then you shall act quickly, for then has gone out Yahweh before you to strike [the] camp of Philistines.

en.L: And let it be, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then you shall act quickly, for then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has gone out before you to strike the camp of [the] Philistines."
en.B: The moment you hear the sound of marching along the tops of the balsam trees, move fast, for that means {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
en.R: As soon as you hear marching up in the tops of the balsam trees, attack at once. That will show that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has gone ahead of you to defeat the Philistine army."

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando oigas el ruido de marcha en las copas de los árboles de bálsamo, entonces actuarás con rapidez, porque entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habrá salido delante de ti para herir el campamento de los filisteos».
es.B: En cuanto oigas el ruido de pasos por las copas de los árboles de bálsamo, muévete rápido, porque eso significa que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha salido delante de ti para derrotar al ejército filisteo».
es.R: Tan pronto como oigas ruido de pasos en lo alto de los árboles de bálsamo, ataca enseguida. Eso te mostrará que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} va delante de ti para derrotar al ejército filisteo».

fr.L: Et qu’il en soit ainsi : quand tu entendras le bruit d’une marche dans la cime des baumiers, alors tu agiras promptement, car alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sera sorti devant toi pour frapper le camp des Philistins. »
fr.B: Dès que tu entendras un bruit de pas à la cime des baumiers, hâte-toi d’agir, car ce sera le signe que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est sorti devant toi pour battre l’armée des Philistins. »
fr.R: Dès que tu entendras un bruit de marche en haut des baumiers, attaque tout de suite. Cela voudra dire que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est parti devant toi pour battre l’armée des Philistins. »

vi.L: Khi nào con nghe tiếng bước chân đi trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, thì hãy hành động mau lẹ, vì lúc ấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra đi trước con để đánh trại quân Phi-li-tin."
vi.B: Ngay khi con nghe tiếng bước quân đi trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, hãy hành động nhanh chóng, vì đó là lúc {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã ra đi trước con để đánh tan quân Phi-li-tin."
vi.R: Ngay khi con nghe tiếng bước quân trên ngọn những cây bóp-ca, hãy tấn công ngay. Điều đó cho biết {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đi trước con để đánh bại quân Phi-li-tin."

decisions.choice: the sound of marching in the treetops: the sign that Yahweh's own army is advancing
decisions.reason: The marching is heard above the trees, where no soldiers walk. It is the sound of Yahweh going out to battle at the head of his heavenly army, as in Judges 4:14 and 5:4. David is to follow where Yahweh has gone first.

decisions.choice: act quickly: move decisively, at once
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut or decide, and here to act with decision and speed, without delay.

decisions.choice: when you hear
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters begin the word with a different preposition from the form marked to be read aloud. Both mean "when you hear"; the read-aloud form is followed here. 1 Chronicles 14:15 has the same words.

decisions.choice: that means (Balanced); That will show (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out that the sound is the sign of Yahweh's going out, which the Hebrew gives with "for then".

en.L: And David did so, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, and he struck [the] Philistines from Geba until you come [to] Gezer.

vi.B: Đa-vít làm đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền lệnh cho ông, và ông đánh người Phi-li-tin suốt từ Ghê-ba đến tận Ghê-xe.

decisions.choice: Geba
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here reads Geba, a town north of Jerusalem in Benjamin. 1 Chronicles 14:16 and the old Greek translation read Gibeon, a town northwest of Jerusalem on the road down to the west; Isaiah 28:21 also names the valley of Gibeon beside Mount Perazim. Gibeon fits the line of flight toward Gezer better, but the Hebrew of Samuel is followed here.

decisions.choice: until your coming to Gezer: as far as Gezer
decisions.reason: "Until you come to" is a way of saying "all the way to" a place (Genesis 10:19). Gezer stood at the edge of the coastal plain; David drove the Philistines out of the hills and back toward their own land.

decisions.choice: David did so, as Yahweh had commanded: obedience, then victory
decisions.reason: The chapter ends with David doing exactly what Yahweh said. Unlike Saul, who did not wait for Yahweh's word (1 Samuel 13:8-14; 15:22-23), David asks and obeys.

decisions.choice: defeated ... and chased them
decisions.reason: Readable splits the verb into "defeated" and "chased", since the Hebrew "struck ... from Geba to Gezer" describes a pursuit across the country.
